Say hello

Good design is quiet. It is why a tired analyst still finds the right answer at 2 a.m.

I'm Chitranssh, a senior product designer and design engineer. I design enterprise products where the screen is dense and the stakes are high: cybersecurity, healthcare, fintech and more. The part I care about most is the gap between the design file and the product that actually ships, so I close it by building what I design.

What I bring

Five things a team gets on day one, each with the project that proves it.

01
Calm screens
I turn dense security and clinical data into a clear hierarchy, so the next action is obvious. On Qualys VMDR, analysts triage vulnerabilities about twice as fast.
02
Systems that hold
Worked on 10+ design systems and built 5 from scratch. I built Quad for Qualys (20+ modules, 40% fewer UI inconsistencies), built one for Northwell, and worked on IBM's design systems.
03
AI people trust
AI guidance that keeps the user in control and can be switched off, so adoption sticks. On IBM CPQ, onboarding time fell 50% and quoting time 35%.
04
Design that ships
Working prototypes in Claude Code and repository-based workflows. Engineering reviews real interaction instead of a static mockup, so the handoff gap closes early.
05
A team that grows
I lead hybrid design teams, mentor junior designers and align stakeholders on one roadmap.

More writing

Small talk

The short ones are here. For anything else, ask the moon.

How did you get into design?

I studied both sides of it: a Bachelor of Fine Arts at Jiwaji University in Gwalior and a Bachelor's in Computer Science at DAVV in Indore. Then a master's in Communication Design at RMIT. Product design is where drawing and logic meet.

What's your main thing?

Enterprise products where the screen is dense and a wrong click costs something: security consoles, clinical data, financial tools. I make the important thing obvious and build the design system that keeps it that way.

Where are you based?

Indore, India. I work across time zones with global clients.

How can I get in touch?

Email trivedichitransh12@gmail.com or message me on LinkedIn. Tell me what you're building and where it's hard.
